rationale: Defines a declarative, framework-neutral contract for agent definitions with shared schemas and runs it on four runtimes; covers only the definition contract, not in-flight checkpoints.

Letta claims Agent File serializes tool definitions, execution environment, model configuration and in-context and external memories for recreation on another server; vendor claim with no reported loss evaluation.
cagent declares models, instructions, toolsets and sub-agents in one YAML file distributed via OCI registries, a vendor example of a portable definition contract.
Memory moves from ChatGPT/Gemini/Copilot to Claude as a user-copied text prompt, so the cross-provider memory unit is a natural-language prompt; the summary reports no measure of what is lost.
Gemini imports memory as a pasted summary and chat history as a ZIP export, two distinct portable units for memory versus conversation.
Cloudflare's ctx.stash() checkpoint and forkable session trees define what an evicted agent resumes from within one platform.
AWS claims agents are defined by configuration, state persists across turns and the harness exports to Strands code; vendor claim without a description of lost fields.

Mecatl is described as resuming a replacement worker from the last persisted turn boundary while in-flight operations are not resumed, an explicit statement of what does and does not move; early, vendor-authored.
Classifies code mobility by what moves (code, execution state, data) and by design paradigm; a pre-LLM vocabulary for separating portable units rather than a contract for LLM agents.
Externalizes agent memory into explicit tiers that can be paged to storage, a prerequisite for a memory-snapshot contract but not itself a transfer format.
Reports that structured intermediate artifacts verified by other agents yield more coherent multi-agent results than free chat, supporting artifacts rather than transcripts as the transferred unit.
Records agent traces and summarizes them into structured multi-level experiences for replay on similar tasks, one candidate portable unit (experience, not live state).
Migrates LLM agents between edge servers by moving only essential state; the summary does not enumerate which fields count as essential.
AIOS kernel provides context management that saves and restores agent context for agents from several frameworks; no field-level portability report in the summary.
Maintains context as a structured, incrementally updated playbook to avoid context collapse, a candidate form for a carried task context.
Compresses observations and interaction history while improving task success, evidence that a compact task context can stand in for full history in at least three benchmarks.
IETF agentproto BoF participants proposed reframing the charter around context propagation across trust boundaries, signalling that the portable unit is still undefined in standards work.
KQML separates a typed message envelope from its content language, the conceptual precedent for an envelope-plus-payload contract.
Defines a mobile agent as suspending, transferring itself and resuming on another host, the classic all-state answer the project explicitly does not assume.
Catalogs state-transfer and residual-dependency problems of process migration that any definition of the moved unit must confront.
Surveys forms and operations of agent memory, a taxonomy from which a memory-snapshot field list could be drawn.

ODIS draft links the principal an agent represents, the authority delegated to it and the specific agent instance acting, i.e. separate identifiers for principal, authority and instance; draft, two early demos.

Proposes IDs for individual AI-system instances (e.g. a session) so parties can attribute incidents and find who can shut it down, directly addressing instance-level identity distinct from the system; position paper.
Microsoft Entra Agent ID (preview) applies audit trails and lifecycle policies per agent; vendor claim reported second-hand.
Google claims each agent receives a cryptographic Agent Identity with auditable authorization policies; vendor keynote claim.
Proposed (not shipped) design encodes the delegation chain in a JWT inside a SPIFFE trust domain, carrying lineage with the executing worker.
An Origin ID field links registered agents to cloud-native identifiers such as AWS ARNs, a vendor mechanism for binding logical agent to physical workload.
Speaks-for calculus with compound principals expresses delegated authority and roles, a formal basis for distinguishing who acts for whom after a handoff.
Grounds agent-communication semantics in publicly observable commitments, giving a verifiable record of who owes what after work changes hands.
Assesses agent identifiers and activity logging as visibility measures, mechanisms for keeping lineage attached to work across operators.
Verifiable agent identities via DIDs/VCs encode provenance and behavioural scope, a mechanism for attesting which agent instance holds a task.
Replay-or-fork semantics on restore implicitly require distinguishing a resumed run from a new fork of the same task.
OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG draft agent semantic conventions aim at framework-neutral telemetry, a substrate for cross-executor trace lineage.

Shows that after checkpoint-restore an LLM agent re-generates slightly different tool requests that servers treat as new (Action Replay), and proposes recording irreversible effects with replay-or-fork semantics; preprint, proof of concept.
Temporal runs the OpenAI Agents SDK loop in Workflows and each model call as an Activity, so retries and crash recovery come from Temporal; vendor integration claim.
DBOS claims to checkpoint every LLM and tool call to Postgres so an agent resumes from its last completed step; vendor claim, no reported duplicate-effect test.
runFiber() registers a durable invocation in SQLite before it runs, an intent-before-execution record within one platform.
States that a replacement worker resumes from the last persisted turn boundary and in-flight operations are not resumed, a conservative design choice rather than a fencing proof.
Implements scheduling and IPC as transactional database operations, the durable-execution foundation that allows resumption on another machine; no agent-specific fencing result.
Proves log-optimal protocols for exactly-once handling of shared-state updates when serverless functions are retried; systems analogue, not LLM agents, and relies on a shared log.
LangGraph 1.0 persists execution state so interrupted runs resume where they stopped; single-framework durability without a stated duplicate-execution guarantee.
Vercel Workflow Development Kit marks retryable steps for suspend/resume; durability primitive without ownership semantics in the summary.
Lambda durable functions checkpoint progress with steps and waits; no statement on concurrent executors or fencing.
Kubernetes Agent Sandbox targets singleton stateful agent workloads with resumption after scale-to-zero, the deployment-level notion of a single active instance.
Process-migration survey covers state transfer and transparency issues that underlie the old-versus-new executor problem.
Names Action Replay as a semantic rollback attack on restored agents and mitigates it by recording irreversible tool effects; directly about re-executed external actions; preprint.
Model and agent invocations run as Temporal Activities with retries; retry semantics are inherited, but the summary gives no idempotency guarantee for external targets.
Shared Payment Token is scoped to one merchant and one cart, which bounds what a replayed payment could charge; the summary says nothing about retries or idempotency.
MCP 2026 roadmap lists retry and expiry semantics for experimental Tasks as a priority, indicating these semantics are not yet defined in the tool protocol.
Claims each tool call is checkpointed and workflows can be forked from a chosen step to avoid repeating costly earlier ones; does not address ambiguous outcomes after timeouts.
In-flight operations are explicitly not resumed after worker replacement, avoiding blind retry but leaving reconciliation unspecified.
Exactly-once semantics for retried functions with external shared state, but within a system that controls the log; does not cover third-party targets that do not cooperate.
AP2 signed Intent and Cart Mandates give an audit trail of user authorization for payments, useful for reconciliation but not a replay-safety mechanism.
x402 'deferred' scheme separates the cryptographic handshake from settlement, a payment-protocol design relevant to when a charge becomes irreversible.
Concludes current identity standards were not designed for recursive delegation chains or cross-domain trust propagation; same whitepaper as AMP-061.

Demonstrates that a second-order prompt injection makes an agent recruit a more capable agent that runs with the initiating user's privileges, letting a low-privileged user read restricted data; vendor research PoC.
Formal speaks-for theory and a built system handling delegation, access control and revocation across RPCs; peer-reviewed foundation.

Macaroons let holders attenuate and delegate credentials by adding contextual caveats, confining how, by whom and in what context authority is exercised; peer-reviewed, pre-LLM but setting-independent.
Extends OAuth 2.0/OIDC with agent-specific credentials so users scope and restrict agent permissions with an accountability chain; preprint (peer-reviewed position successor noted in corpus).
Proposes fine-grained dynamic access control and a session/policy layer for consistent revocation across agent protocols; peer-reviewed design.
OpenID Foundation whitepaper sets out delegated authority and scalable access control for agents as open problems; same document as AMN-040.
SAGA derives fine-grained access-control tokens with formal guarantees for inter-agent communication and reports minimal overhead in evaluation; peer-reviewed system.
Mastercard Agentic Tokens require registered agents and consumer control of what an agent may buy; vendor claim.
Windows MCP proxy requires user approval of each client-tool pair and centralizes consent and authentication; preview with some controls not yet enforced.
Okta Cross App Access has the enterprise IdP check policy and issue a token the target app validates; vendor claim.
AgentCore Identity binds credentials to agent-user pairs and supports acting as the agent or on behalf of a user; vendor claim.
AP2 mandates are signed proofs of user authorization scoped to intent and cart.
Shared Payment Token lets an agent start a payment without seeing buyer credentials, scoped to one merchant and one cart, a concrete narrow expiring-grant pattern.
Auth0 Token Vault and CIBA asynchronous human-in-the-loop authorization for agents; vendor claim of re-issuance and approval flows.
District court found access likely unauthorized because it had the user's permission but not Amazon's, showing user-delegated authority may not bind third parties.
MCP 2026-07-28 binds client credentials to the issuing server and adds RFC 9207 issuer validation, guarding the 'wrong audience' case.
Appeals panel vacated that injunction, finding on the current record the assistant acted as a tool on the user's instructions; legal status of delegated agent authority remains unsettled.
MCP roadmap targets an agent identity and delegation path via Workload Identity Federation, ID-JAG and token exchange; planned, not shipped.
ODIS draft extends OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SPIFFE and SCIM to link principal, delegated authority and agent instance across trust domains.
Proposed design encodes the delegation chain in a JWT; not yet shipped.
SPIFFE identities and short-lived tokens issued to agents to replace static credentials; vendor claim.
Formal analysis of OAuth 2.0 found four practical attacks and proved the fixed protocol secure in its model, bounding what OAuth-based agent delegation can claim.
Frames delegation as transfer of authority, responsibility and accountability with explicit role boundaries; conceptual framework without evaluation.
CaMeL attaches capabilities to values and enforces policy at tool-call time, a mechanism for narrowing what a receiving executor may do with data.
NIST NCCoE concept paper solicits input on identifying, authorizing and auditing software agents.
NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative names agent identity and security research as a pillar.
Applies principal-agent theory and agency law to AI agents, framing discretionary authority and liability.
Argues for shared agent infrastructure that attributes actions to agents and users.
Agent session smuggling over A2A extracted the client agent's system instructions, tool schemas and chat history in a PoC; no in-the-wild attacks reported.
Agent card poisoning made a host send full booking payload including payment card details to an attacker endpoint before delegation (simulated scenario).
Demonstrates that retrieved content acts as instructions (data theft, worm-like spreading) on deployed LLM applications; any context crossing a boundary is such content; peer-reviewed.
InjecAgent quantifies indirect prompt injection including private-data exfiltration across 30 agents; ReAct GPT-4 compromised in about a quarter of cases.
AgentDojo provides an extensible harness for injections carried in tool outputs, with attacks and defences; the reference environment for canary-style leakage tests.
ASB shows memory poisoning and attacks at every stage including memory retrieval succeed often with limited defences, so carried memory needs integrity checks.
Adversarial content hijacks inter-agent control flow, leading to code execution or exfiltration from containers in 58-90% of GPT-4o trials.
Adversarial self-replicating prompts contaminate other applications' retrieval stores and extract confidential data, each client compromising about 20 others within 1-3 days.
CaMeL blocks exfiltration over unauthorised data flows by design, solving 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security vs 84% undefended.
Prompt injection propagates agent-to-agent in multi-agent systems enabling data theft; adapted defences reduce spread.
Tool poisoning made an agent read SSH keys and config and send them to an attacker server; leakage through tool metadata.
Comet browser agent passed webpage content to the LLM unseparated; a hidden comment exfiltrated email and OTP; single-agent, not cross-agent.
ForcedLeak: instructions hidden in a CRM form field caused Agentforce to exfiltrate CRM data via an expired allowlisted domain; single-agent incident.
Argues filesystem plus network isolation is needed to contain a prompt-injected agent; vendor claim of 84% fewer permission prompts.
Imported memories can be reviewed and edited by the user, a consent control on cross-provider memory transfer.
Public red-teaming found at least one successful hijack against every one of 13 frontier models, with some attacks transferring across models.
Gemini memory import excludes Business, Enterprise and under-18 accounts and the EEA, UK and Switzerland; the summary gives no reason, but it signals jurisdictional/consent limits on moving memory.
Atlas memories are described as optional and manageable with opt-out, a consent posture for agent memory.
OWASP Agentic Top 10 lists Memory and Context Poisoning and Insecure Inter-Agent Communication as risk categories.
IETF participants proposed a signaling protocol for managing context across trust boundaries.
Agent File moves serialized agent state between Letta servers (cloud and local); same framework on both ends.
Temporal supplies its own implementation of the OpenAI Agents SDK Runner, showing one framework's loop hosted on another durability substrate.
Agent Spec definitions run on LangGraph, WayFlow and CrewAI and stream to any AG-UI frontend; vendor claim, definitions only.
Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 offers checkpointing/hydration plus migration assistants that analyse Semantic Kernel and AutoGen code; code migration, not checkpoint migration.
DBOS makes an OpenAI Agents SDK agent durable through a native integration, another cross-substrate composition.
AWS claims one CLI command exports the harness to Strands-based code (Claude Agent SDK export 'coming soon'); unclear whether runtime state is included.
Ontolingua translates one ontology into several representation systems, the classic precedent for adapter-based translation with representation-specific loss.
Measures cold, pre-copy, post-copy and hybrid container migration on a fog testbed; runtime-level, framework-agnostic but same software on both ends.
Transparent CPU+GPU snapshots via CRIU with much shorter recovery than prior work; process-level checkpoint, not cross-framework.
AIOS serves agents from several frameworks with kernel-level context save/restore; no cross-framework loss report in the summary.
Runs one declarative agent definition on LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen and WayFlow with a cross-runtime evaluation harness; definition portability, not in-flight checkpoint migration.
Proposes a framework-agnostic mitigation for checkpoint-restore hazards; about safe restore, not cross-framework state translation.
Memory Bank is a managed memory service callable from ADK, LangGraph and CrewAI, so memory can be shared across frameworks without migrating execution state.
ACP-to-A2A migration via adapters and a migration guide is a protocol migration, not state migration.
LangGraph persistence resumes interrupted runs within LangGraph only.
MCP roadmap lists configuration portability under enterprise readiness, with no working group yet.
Process-migration survey explains low adoption due to residual dependencies, a cautionary precedent.
Cross-provider memory import to Claude via a text prompt takes about 24 hours to absorb; no measurement of preserved intent.
Gemini lets users continue imported conversations from other providers; no reported continuity quality.
AWS claims providers can be switched mid-session without losing context; no quality or drift data given.
DSPy separates a declarative pipeline from model-specific prompts and recompiles per model, including smaller open models, implying prompts do not transfer unchanged across models.
MAST annotates traces from seven frameworks across models and finds inter-agent misalignment failures such as lost context and ignored inputs.
AgentRR proposes replaying recorded experiences across large-small model collaboration with check functions as safety anchors; position paper, no cross-model drift numbers.
Cross-runtime evaluation harness compares behaviour of the same definition across runtimes; varies runtime rather than model.
cagent declares models as swappable across providers; no evaluation.
Microsoft Agent Framework accepts any IChatClient so model providers can be swapped without code changes; says nothing about behavioural equivalence.
Attacks found on more robust models transferred to less robust ones but not the reverse, another model-dependence result.
CAMEL inception prompting keeps an executing agent aligned with instructor intent, framing intent preservation between agents.
Mem0 stores memory as a service decoupled from any single model, enabling but not evaluating model change.
Finds more capable models often more susceptible to tool poisoning, evidence that safety behaviour differs by model.
Documents tool poisoning, 'rug pulls' (server changes tool descriptions after approval) and tool shadowing; recommends tool pinning.
A malicious or hijacked MCP server returned a crafted OAuth endpoint that gave command execution on the connecting client (CVE-2025-6514).
postmark-mcp impersonated a legitimate MCP server and after 15 clean versions began BCC-ing all email to an attacker.
Malicious remote A2A agent exploited implicit inter-agent trust; recommended mitigations include signed agent cards and out-of-band approval.
Agent card poisoning: adversarial instructions hidden in a remote agent's A2A Agent Card led the host to disclose payment data to an attacker; directly a fake/hostile capability advertisement.
OX Security claims 9 of 11 MCP registries accepted poisoned entries in testing; vendor research claim.
ANS registry gives PKI-verified agent identity, capability-aware resolution and a threat analysis; peer-reviewed design.
VCs encode capabilities, provenance, behavioural scope and security posture, i.e. attested rather than self-advertised capabilities.
Static analysis of 1,899 MCP servers finds 5.5% with tool poisoning and 7.2% with general vulnerabilities.
Peer-reviewed MAESTRO threat model of A2A emphasizing Agent Card management, task-execution integrity and authentication.
Prototype uses DIDs and third-party VCs to establish cross-domain trust; reports feasibility and limitations when the LLM alone controls security procedures.
MCPTox benchmarks poisoned tool metadata on live MCP servers across 20 agent settings; agents almost never refuse.
Windows MCP registry requires code signing, immutable tool definitions and security testing; preview.
AGNTCY provides agent discovery (OASF) and cryptographic agent identity.
A2A v0.3 added the ability to sign agent cards and a Technology Compatibility Kit.
MCP Registry maintainers can denylist servers reported for malicious code or impersonation; preview without durability guarantees.
GoDaddy ANS trust chain combines domain validation, DNSSEC, DANE pinning and transparency logs; developer preview announced.
Default-on agent discovery let an injected prompt recruit a more capable agent, showing discovery itself is an attack surface.
A2A v1.0 adds Signed Agent Cards for cryptographic identity; signatures attest origin, not honesty of advertised capabilities.
Frames the untrusted-host problem for mobile agents and proposes computing with encrypted functions; classic and narrow.
NIST threat model includes threats from platforms to agents with countermeasures; pre-LLM.
MCPSafetyScanner audits an MCP server's tools before deployment.
Lifecycle threat taxonomy of MCP servers across four attacker types and 16 scenarios.
W3C community group scope includes discovery, capability exchange and verifiable credentials.
Cloudflare verifies agent traffic via Web Bot Auth signatures and de-listed undeclared crawlers, the reverse direction (destination verifying the agent).
Visa Trusted Agent Protocol lets merchants verify agent signatures; reverse direction.
IETF DAWN BoF on decentralized agent discovery; no outcomes reported.
Survey organizes agent threats around interaction with untrusted external entities, framing destination-trust risks without a specific mechanism.
Users grant or revoke per-site access and Claude confirms high-risk actions; vendor claim, no race analysis.
MCP 2025-11-25 experimental Tasks define working, input-required, completed, failed and cancelled states; states, not guarantees about side effects.
MCP roadmap prioritizes retry and expiry semantics for Tasks, confirming they were undefined.
Lists interruptibility and approval requirements as baseline practices, with open questions on operationalizing them.
Instance IDs help identify who can shut a system down, a precondition for targeted cancellation.
Proposes consistent revocation across agent protocols via a unified session/policy layer; credential revocation, not in-flight action cancellation.
Recording irreversible tool effects supplies the information needed for non-rollback warnings after cancellation.
Singapore framework requires human approval at checkpoints.
MCP 2026-07-28 moves Tasks into an extension (SEP-2663).
In-flight operations are not resumed after worker replacement; silent on cancellation.
Formal treatment includes revocation of delegated authority.
UCP manifests at /.well-known/ucp declare services, capabilities and payment handlers; domain-specific capability declaration.
A2A v1.0 adds version negotiation and lets an agent card advertise v0.3 and v1.0; syntactic, not semantic, compatibility.
MCP requests now carry protocol version, client identity and capabilities in _meta with optional server/discover; capability declaration without semantic checks.
Shared ontologies translated across representation systems address meaning preservation, the classic semantic-compatibility approach.
Argues semantics based on private mental states are unverifiable in open systems and should rest on observable commitments, relevant to what can be negotiated and checked.
HuggingGPT routes subtasks by models' textual function descriptions, showing capability claims drive delegation without verification.
Agora lets agents negotiate standardized routines, natural language or LLM-written routines and copes with changing interfaces; protocol-level, not policy or memory-semantics negotiation.
Agent integration protocol and dynamic teaming for heterogeneous third-party agents.
Capability-aware name resolution in ANS.
W3C CG scope covers capability exchange and web-native agent metadata.
MCP roadmap plans .well-known metadata so capabilities are discoverable without a live connection.
Moving from A2A v0.3 to v1 requires code changes, an example of breaking protocol evolution.
IETF agentproto BoF rejected the initial scope 38-124, showing no consensus on what to standardize.
Compares KQML and FIPA ACL formal semantics and notes open conversation-policy issues.

Injected prompts copy themselves agent to agent; defences reduce spread.

Contract Net announce-bid-award protocol for distributing tasks among nodes.

Dynamically adjusts agent-group composition during a task.
Self-organizing memory notes that update each other, relevant to divergent memory but not to merging copies.

Appellate panel treated the assistant as a tool acting on the user's instructions, bearing on who answers for agent conduct; limited to the record.
Proposes attributability, approval and legibility of activity as baseline governance practices.
Assesses agent identifiers, real-time monitoring and activity logging across centralized and decentralized supply chains, including privacy implications.

Agent infrastructure for attributing actions and detecting and remedying harm.

Claims forking from a chosen step avoids repeating costly earlier steps; vendor claim, no numbers.
Explains why process migration saw little adoption despite clear benefits.

Identifies which container migration technique suits which network and service conditions.

Reports substantially lower deployment latency and migration cost for LLM agents on edge servers; compared with other placement strategies, not with restart or delegation.
